//: Plan §6.6. A capability the engine advertises (mobile/ENGINE_DEFAULT.json, or the Swift `advertisedCapabilities` literal) requires zero swift-pending cases and zero unported tests in every family listed under it; coverage.test.js enforces that. Every family a fixture or an unported entry uses must appear under some capability, so no family can hold owed work that no gate reads. `compare` (NE-05) is the comparator's own table, not a rule of the product: it sits under EVERY capability because each one's verdicts are only as good as the Swift comparator that produced them. `remainder` (NE-14j) is the M3 manager remainder NE-39j records (plan §6 families table: about 70 queue-manager scenarios, milestone M3): it is charged here, not to episode or foray, because those capabilities ship in M1 and M2 and must not wait on M3 work. No build advertises it — engine-contract.js CAPABILITIES does not even allow it in a hello — and NE-39s empties it and deletes the lists. `prepare-narration` (NE-45j) waits here too: it is a foray rule (the prepare family's seams with a narration line in them), but the M2 build advertises foray and cannot owe NE-45s's port, so NE-45s moves it to foray (or folds it into prepare) in the PR that empties it. `route-resume` (NE-38rj) waits here too: it is an episode rule (a car resumes whatever was playing), but the M2 build advertises episode and cannot owe NE-38rs's port, so NE-38rs moves it to episode in the PR that empties it. `foray-data` (NE-30j) is the page's build of real Forays, JS only (schema jsOnly): charged to foray so the family is gated like every other, and it can never hold a pending id.
